published.citation: Todorov et al. 2012, dayside brightness temperature at 3.6 µm (NASA Exoplanet Archive emission table): 1923 +/- 56 K, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2012ApJ...746..111T/abstract

temperature.note: Its day side's brightness temperature is measured in secondary eclipse at 3.6 µm (Spitzer Space Telescope satellite Infrared Array Camera (IRAC)) and nobody has imaged it, so the color is a Planck spectrum at its published temperature.
temperature.chosen: 2 measured of 2 rows; the smallest relative uncertainty, then the longest wavelength
temperature.facility: Spitzer Space Telescope satellite Infrared Array Camera (IRAC)
